summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog polls a hardcoded HTTP server and executes returned commands as child processes
details: The package ships a `tt-help watchdog` CLI subcommand that polls an HTTP server's `/api/watchdog/heartbeat` endpoint and passes each element of the response's `commands` array to `child_process.spawn` (with `shell: true` on Windows) via a process-manager routine. The server URL is read from `~/.tt-help.json`, and the help text documents an example server at `http://117.71.53.99:17301`. Whoever controls that server obtains arbitrary command execution on the host running the watchdog, with auto-restart and threshold-based re-spawn logic. Additionally, while the watchdog is running, `checkForUpdates()` polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and, on a newer version, invokes `child_process.exec("npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest")` and restarts — pulling any future author-published version onto the host without operator confirmation. Harm is gated behind the user explicitly running the `watchdog` subcommand (it does not fire on `npm install` or on `require()`), but once started the remote server has a persistent command channel into the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
